newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media see Chirac warned, wait for 2nd round.
newsitem.headline: German media see Chirac warned, wait for 2nd round.

text.p: German media said the left-wing victory in the first round of France's parliamentary elections was a sensational slap at President Jacques Chirac but warned voters could still turn to the right in the second round.

Radio and television reports on the vote, the first item in most news broadcasts, used words like "devastating," "shocking" and "sensational" to describe the 4.5-point lead the left won over the unpopular government coalition parties.

Juergen Trittin, spokesman of the Greeens party, said the result was a clear protest against neo-liberal policies and hoped the "red-green alliance" of Socialists, Greens and Communists would win the second round as well.
Financial analysts expressed surprise but advised caution until the final result emerges after the second round of voting next Sunday.
"I didn't expect it to swing this much," said Rudolf Chimelli, Paris correspondent for Munich's Sueddeutsche Zeitung, in a commentary for N-TV television.
"It is a protest vote. But nothing is less solid than the assumption that the French will behave the same way next Sunday as they have this Sunday."
German Radio called the result "sensational" and asked whether Chirac would be able to hold onto Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Analyst Valerie Wilhelm from Societe Generale in Paris said the size of the left-wing surge was a surprise.
"I hope it will not have an effect on the stock market -- remember this is only the first round," she told N-TV.
"We will have to watch very carefully what plans for change the government parties can present this week."
The strongest commentary came from West German Radio in Cologne, which called the result a debacle for Chirac and "more than just a warning."

"The real loser is Jacques Chirac, who has managed to provoke such a defeat just two years after taking office," it said. "It is questionable if a president can govern effectively on such a narrow popular basis.
"The political va banque game of the Gaullist gambler has not brought the desired effect."

The West German Radio commentary went on: "The extent of the debacle becomes clear when one realises that the two conservative parties of the Chirac coalition together won only 31.5 percent. That is less than a third of the votes cast.

"Chirac has risked a political 'fuite en avance' but this has led him into a dead end. The Chirac coalition has run out of steam more quickly than expected and the left has gained political strength again."

The Westfaelische Nachrichten newspaper said: "French voters have let off some steam. The government parties ... could not communicate two things to the voters -- the purpose of a vote right now and whether they were competent to solve the problems France faces."
The Frankfurter Rundschau daily commented: "Jacques Chirac has miscalculated and his surprise attack has gone wrong."

Bonn's General-Anzeiger said voters had "corrected a democratic deficit" in the first round and recalled the government parties had held a four-fifths majority in the National Assembly that Chirac dissolved to hold the vote.
"There could not be an effective opposition. This situation, which is impossible for a proud democracy to bear, has been ended."
